stories.about: Drafted answers in each prep pack are stitched from these. Facts only, from the resume and interview prep: edit any of them, and never add a number you cannot back up.

proud.jiraAgent: At Kynetec I was handed a one-sentence brief with no spec: see whether AI can help the team get through Jira tickets faster. I narrowed it to the question everything depended on - can an agent write an implementation plan an engineer would actually trust? - and built that. Every night the agent reads the team's assigned tickets, investigates the codebase with read-only tools, deciding which files to search and read from what it has just found, and writes a plan that says what it would change and what it was unsure about. An engineer approves or rejects it from a Teams card in under two minutes. It runs on Claude via Bedrock, orchestrated by two Airflow DAGs with the plans kept in Postgres, with guardrails from day one: per-run cost ceilings, iteration caps and an audit of every tool call.
proud.unmarked: Unmarked is a football decision-training app I built solo, from idea to production, with Claude Code - to help my son read his positioning on the pitch. Young players drag their off-the-ball run in 40+ frozen match moments and are graded the way a coach would grade it. The part I'm proudest of is the rules engine: instead of one right answer per scenario, declarative coach cards (30 rule types) compute the great and good areas, and one TypeScript engine drives the app, a build-time validator and a self-auditing review page, so content can't drift from the rules that grade it. It runs as an offline-first PWA with a Three.js pitch tuned on real phones.
proud.qala: The Qala is an online store I built end to end for a handmade jewellery brand. Orders from the site, WhatsApp and Instagram land in one order book behind signed, rate-limited logins. The owner has a content studio: products are uploaded with photos and video, images are shrunk in the browser and committed to GitHub, and an automated build regenerates the catalogue and redeploys the site on Cloudflare. It is a whole product - storefront, operations and publishing - owned by one engineer.
proud.pettrak: PetTrak turns de-identified clinic transaction data into standardised market insights for animal health clients. I built its React front end - dashboards for market insights, clinic metrics and product performance - designed the Databricks pipelines that turn curated gold-layer datasets into the data products behind its APIs and reporting, added Lambda functions for event-driven processing, and orchestrate the workflows in Airflow. As team lead I own the design decisions on the platform and the standards the team codes to.
proud.langley: At Synechron I worked on Langley for Asurion, an enterprise platform that pulls information from disparate sources into a search-driven UI on AWS OpenSearch over PostgreSQL. I ran requirement gathering directly with the client, closed the design gaps and owned the architecture, built serverless applications in React, Node and Python on AWS, and set up CI/CD with Docker, Jenkins and GitHub Actions, with Terraform for the infrastructure.

stories.toughCall: On the Jira planning agent, the obvious goal was an agent that writes code. I decided the first version would stop at a plan, with read-only tools only. Nobody was going to let an agent change our codebase until they trusted its thinking, and a plan is cheap to review and cheap to throw away while still testing the hard part: does it understand the code well enough to know what to change? It also made the pilot safe by construction - the worst outcome is a bad plan that an engineer rejects. I split it into two Airflow DAGs with the human approval in between, and execution writes only to prefixed feature branches, never main.
stories.ambiguity: The Jira planning agent started as a one-sentence brief: no spec, no level of autonomy, no definition of good. I narrowed it to the single question everything depended on - can an agent write a plan an engineer would trust? - built the smallest thing that could answer it, a plan only, with read-only tools and guardrails, and piloted it on one team, with config-driven onboarding for wider rollout.
stories.ai: I build with AI as well as use it. At Kynetec I designed an autonomous Jira planning agent on Claude via Bedrock: a tool-calling loop, a human approval gate, cost ceilings, iteration caps and a full audit trail. Outside work I built Unmarked from idea to production with Claude Code, and The Qala with Claude. The lesson I keep relearning: AI is fastest when the guardrails come first - read-only tools, limits, audits, a validator that gates generated content - so what it produces can be trusted.
stories.remote: I work remotely from India with teams and clients across the US and UK, so async, written-first collaboration is how I already operate. I overlap 3.5-4.5 hours with CET and 1.5-3 hours with the UK.
stories.stack: 15+ years overall, hands-on throughout. Front end: React, Redux, Next.js, JavaScript, TypeScript and Tailwind - my day-to-day stack. Back end: Node, Python with FastAPI, REST APIs and PostgreSQL. Data: Databricks, Apache Airflow, Kafka, Elasticsearch and OpenSearch. Cloud: AWS (Lambda, S3, EC2, API Gateway, CloudFront, CloudWatch), Terraform and Docker, with CI/CD on GitHub Actions and Jenkins. Recently: LLM agents on Claude via Bedrock.
